items.title: Sidebar advises KP Group on majority stake acquisition in DEK and Mavericks Green Energy
items.summary: Sun Drops Energia Private Limited, a KP Group company, has acquired a majority stake in DEK and Mavericks Green Energy Limited. The transaction has been structured through a share swap arrangement, pursuant to which Sun Drops Energia will acquire shares of DEK and Mavericks Green Energy from its existing shareholders under a Share Swap Agreement. As consideration for the acquisition, compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) of Sun Drops Energia will be issued to the selling shareholders. Sidebar advised KP Group and Sun Drops Energia on the transaction, including the transaction structure, legal and regulatory aspects, due diligence, negotiation and finalisation of the Share Swap Agreement and other transaction documents, and matters relating to the issuance of CCPS. The transaction team was led by Purusharth Singh (Founding Partner). The transaction was led for KP Group by Karmit Sheth (Head – Legal, KP Group of Companies). items.title: Distribute samosas and tea to DHCBA employees: Delhi High Court to lawyers as condition to waive costs
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed counsel for a litigant to distribute chai and samosa to Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) employees as condition to do away with costs imposed by it earlier. In an order passed on September 17, Justice Saurabh Banerjee directed the lawyers for the petitioner to comply with the direction within one week. "The present application is disposed of, however, learned counsel for the petitioners is called upon to distribute samosas and tea to all the employees of Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) within a period of one week." Justice Saurabh Banerjee and Delhi High Court The matter pertained to cheque bounce case against the petitioner company, Indus Birra Beverages and its officials. The company was seeking quashing of the criminal complaint under Negotiable Instruments Act. On August 20, the Court had dismissed the petition and imposed costs of ₹50,000 on the petitioers for not making full disclosure of a trial court order. They then filed an application to waive the costs. The Court allowed the same on September 17 subject to the lawyers distributing tea and samosas to DHCBA employees.
